misconceptions.description: Using verbs like understand, appreciate, be familiar with, or be aware of as if they specify a testable performance
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes 'learners will understand X' as a complete objective
misconceptions.feedback: Replace unmeasurable verbs with Bloom-aligned action verbs (explain, classify, compute, defend, design, critique). If you cannot test it, you cannot teach to it.

misconceptions.description: Believing that any assessment item can validate any objective regardless of cognitive level
misconceptions.trigger: learner pairs a recall question with an Evaluate-level objective
misconceptions.feedback: Constructive alignment requires the assessment to operate at the same Bloom level as the objective. A recall item cannot validate an Evaluate or Create objective.

misconceptions.description: Combining multiple performances at multiple cognitive levels into a single objective for brevity
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes 'analyze and evaluate and design' in one objective
misconceptions.feedback: Each Bloom level deserves its own objective so that assessment, practice, and feedback can be designed precisely. Split stacked objectives into separate, single-verb objectives.

misconceptions.description: Treating constructive alignment as an end-of-project documentation task rather than a design discipline
misconceptions.trigger: learner says 'we'll align after we build it'
misconceptions.feedback: Alignment is the design move that prevents wasted work. Misaligned objectives, activities, and assessments mean parts of the course are teaching or testing the wrong thing entirely.
